item.title: Colts GM Chris Ballard on Keenan Allen DUI arrest: 'He's a tremendous human being. Give him some grace'
item.description: Chris Ballard defended Keenan Allen after his DUI arrest, citing Philip Rivers' endorsement and a decorated 14-year NFL career without issues.
item.content:encoded:
Keenan Allen remains with the Indianapolis Colts following a DUI arrest Sunday and, from listening to general manager Chris Ballard address the matter on Tuesday, that's not going to change anytime soon.

"Good people make mistakes, OK?" Ballard said in articulating an initial defense for keeping the veteran wide receiver on the roster heading into the team's regular-season opener against the Baltimore Ravens.

"He's a tremendous human being. Give him some grace. And he'll work through the process of the legal system."

So, it is clear that is what the Colts intend to do.

Allen was a late training camp addition because the Colts decided they needed insurance against Alec Pierce's return to health from a lingering calf and heel issue.

ANTHONY RICHARDSON'S TURNOVERS IN PRESEASON OPENER RAISE MORE QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS COLTS FUTURE

He signed a one-year contract on Aug. 19 and it made sense because the 34-year-old wide receiver is reuniting with head coach Shane Steichen, who previously worked with Allen in Los Angeles.

Allen also came with an endorsement from Philip Rivers, who played for the Colts previously and after Daniel Jones was injured last year. Rivers and Allen were teammates with the Chargers.

And that history is a major reason Ballard is defending Allen.

"Fourteen years in a league, no issues, OK?" Ballard said. "Decorated career, decorated teammate, as you know, our relationship with Philip Rivers. I know Philip holds him in extremely high regard, and Shane was with him.

"And after you meet his his mom and dad who are just amazing people, we feel good about who he is.

"Unequivocally."

Allen played in only one preseason game for the Colts after being signed. But hours after that preseason appearance Saturday, he was arrested at approximately 1 a.m., Sunday in downtown Indianapolis.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department said officers investigated after seeing Allen's vehicle parked in a no-parking zone in the 100 block of South Meridian Street and reported signs of intoxication.

PRO BOWL RUNNING BACK MILES SANDERS ARRESTED ON DUI CHARGES, COURT RECORDS SHOW

Allen was booked on preliminary misdemeanor charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated while endangering another person and operating a vehicle with a blood-alcohol concentration of at least 0.08%.

Authorities have not publicly disclosed Allen’s precise blood-alcohol reading.

Allen was transported to the Marion County Arrestee Processing Center, with records indicating he was released at 3:49 p.m., Sunday. No bond amount has been publicly reported.

The Marion County Prosecutor’s Office will make the final charging decision on Allen, while the NFL continues to monitor the situation, according to a league source. Allen could be subject to discipline under the league's Personal Conduct Policy.

The NFL has quite a few Personal Conduct Policy issues pending.

Allen's first scheduled court date is Sept. 16, three days after the Colts' regular-season opener against the Ravens.

item.title: Penta clinches World Heavyweight Championship match vs Roman Reigns after epic brawl with Rey Fenix
item.description: Penta defeated Rey Fenix in a thrilling "Monday Night Raw" tournament final to earn a World Heavyweight Championship shot against Roman Reigns.
item.content:encoded:
Penta and Rey Fenix delivered one of the most exciting matches on "Monday Night Raw" this year as the two top Luchadores in the sport battled for a shot at a world title.

Penta and Fenix were the final two competitors in the World Heavyweight Championship No. 1 Contender’s Tournament. The winner would receive an opportunity to face Roman Reigns in Mexico City on Sept. 14.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

On Monday, Penta and Fenix showcased the good that comes along with professional wrestling – two men who know each other very well battling it out with important stakes attached. That’s what fans in Cleveland and those watching on Netflix got to see.

The two went blow-for-blow almost immediately out of the gate. Each of their high-risk, high-reward moves being outdone by what came next. Fenix, at one point countered an avalanche Mexican destroyer attempt, stunning Penta and turning it around into a Mexican muscle buster.

It wasn’t long before the two needed to go on the outside of the ring to inflict pain. Fenix was going for a kill shot on the announcers’ desk. But Penta turned it around on him and sent Fenix through the table with a Penta Driver. The two competitors crashed through the table, leaving the fans stunned.

Penta got Fenix back into the ring. He worked on Fenix’s arm and set him up for one more devastating Mexican destroyer. He pinned Fenix to win the tournament and to get his chance at WWE glory.

Roman Reigns entered the ring before the show was over and got face-to-face with Penta. It will be a match that Reigns will really have to prepare for. Reigns has gone toe-to-toe with the best that WWE has to offer – Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Brock Lesnar, John Cena and more. But there’s not much he’ll be able to do to match what Penta does in the ring.

It would be really something if Penta, somehow, walks out of Mexico City as the world heavyweight champion. Reigns’ recent run as champion has been dominant. But with the summer closing, could Penta possibly upset Reigns in one of the biggest spots of his career since joining WWE? Only time will tell.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Fenix may have lost to Penta on Raw but there are still big things ahead for him.

He will be a part of Triplemania 34 – a two night spectacle showcasing the incredible roster of Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (AAA). The first night will take place in Las Vegas on Sept. 11 and the second will be held in Mexico City on Sept. 13.

Fenix is set to defend the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship against Jack Cartwheel, Mini Vikingo and Nathan Frazer.

His three opponents battled each other at Ola De Calor on Sunday afternoon to see who will become the No. 1 contender for the title. However, the match reached a time limit. Fenix came out and announced he would take on all three at Triplemania.

item.title: Woke stunt goes horribly wrong as Michigan Dems open convention with brutal ‘land acknowledgment’
item.description: The Michigan Democratic Convention opened with a botched land acknowledgement as vice chair Portia Roberson struggled to pronounce Anishinaabe names.
item.content:encoded:
LANSING, Mich. — A woke stunt went horribly wrong at Sunday’s Democratic Party Nominating Convention in Michigan as a top official opened the event with a brutal attempt at a "land acknowledgment."

"I am here to offer our land acknowledgment," said Portia Roberson, the vice chair of the state's party, at the outset of the afternoon gathering of Democrats. "Our land acknowledgments in Michigan recognize the state as the ancestral, traditional and contemporary land of the Anishinaabe, Three Fires Confederacy — "

But she was cut off after an incorrect pronunciation of Anishinaabe when several audience members began shouting the correct pronunciation at Roberson, to which she replied, "Say it again for me."

OBAMA CENTER EMBEDS 'INDIGENOUS' LAND MESSAGE ON CONTROVERSIAL SITE

"Stand up," Roberson then told a woman wearing a white t-shirt in the crowd. "You do it better than me. Make it — I'm big on names being pronounced right, so make sure I get it right."

The audience member then repeated the pronunciation of the word Anishinaabe until Roberson successfully mimicked it into the microphone.

"Thank you. Wait, don't sit down yet," she told the convention-goer. "I might get another one wrong. You may have to correct me, and I want to get this right."

OBAMA PRESIDENTIAL CENTER FOLLOWS WIDELY MOCKED 'STOLEN LAND' ACKNOWLEDGMENT WITH NATIVE AMERICAN DANCE SHOW

She then picked up where she left off.

"Including the Odawa, Ottawa, Ojibwe, Chippewa and ... Potawatomi," she said, sparking another round of audience shouting with a mispronunciation of the last tribe.

"See, usually I rehearse before I come out. This time I rushed it and I didn't rehearse. I apologize," Roberson admitted before exiting the stage.

The Democratic Party of Michigan did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment about the land acknowledgment or Roberson's pronunciation mishaps.

Land acknowledgments have become a woke ritual for those aiming to placate the far-left by recognizing where an event is held or institution is located is on land that was originally inhabited by Indigenous people — with the implication that the land was 'stolen' from them.

JEWISH AG’S CONVENTION BOYCOTT EXPOSES DEEPENING ISRAEL FAULT LINE AMONG MICHIGAN DEMOCRATS

The convention room inside the Lansing Center, where the event was held over the weekend, was about half-full as Michigan's Democratic nominees for statewide office paraded onto the stage one-by-one.

Each gave a brief speech surrounded by supporters holding campaign memorabilia.

The convention's largest draw was embattled Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive who mostly lashed out at President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance over economic issues, and stumped for socialized healthcare.

EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS

Trump was also invoked by several of the candidates.

Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, who is running for governor, Michigan Senate Majority Leader Winnie Brinks, Benson's nominee for lieutenant governor and Lt. Gov. Garlin Gilchrist, a software engineer who is running for Secretary of State, were a few of the major attractions of the convention.

"When I’m secretary of state, your data will belong to you," he said, "not the federal government."

Brinks focused her ire on Rep. John James, R-Mich.

"Time and time again, James has made it clear that he is not fighting for the people of Michigan," she said. "He’s fighting for Donald Trump."

Gilchrist said he'd protect Michiganders' data from the federal government, which is seeking voter rolls in several states.

item.title: Red state heartlands put a ring on young love while progressive blue cities lag on early marriage
item.description: IFS research reveals young adults in their 20s marry at far higher rates in middle America than in New York or Los Angeles metro areas.
item.content:encoded:
Young people looking to tie the knot in their 20s may want to rethink where they live. Moving to big coastal cities like New York and Los Angeles could mean lowering the odds of getting married — and living in an area with a high concentration of singles may not lead to more marriages.

According to a new study from the Institute for Family Studies (IFS), early-marriage rates are lower in many urban hubs and higher in parts of the heartland. The findings point to a geographical divide in family formation, with young adults in places like Tennessee, Indiana and Utah marrying at higher rates than their coastal big-city peers.

"For singles, your best odds of finding love and getting married aren’t in big coastal cities where most singles live, but in middle America, where more marriage‑minded singles are," Wendy Wang, senior researcher at the Institute for Family Studies, told Fox News Digital.

THE STATES REVEALED AS BEST TO START A FAMILY AMID CRATERING BELIEF IN THE AMERICAN DREAM

The research is part of the IFS’s "Get Married Maps," which provides young people with information about regional marriage trends and examines factors associated with marriage rates. Those factors include employment, religion and recent presidential election results, among others.

"Given the many benefits of marriage, a city where more young people are tying the knot might ultimately provide a more fulfilling life than one with just excellent entertainment and tasty food—but few weddings," the study explains.

For adults ages 22-29, regions with the highest marriage rates include Provo, Utah, as well as parts of Tennessee, Indiana, Nebraska, Kentucky, Idaho, North Carolina, Kansas and Georgia. In contrast, eight of the 10 regions with the lowest early-marriage rates are concentrated in the New York and Los Angeles metropolitan areas.

NORTH TEXAS DOMINATES IN POPULATION GROWTH AS BIG BLUE CITIES FAIL TO RECOVER TO PRE-PANDEMIC LEVELS

"These findings demonstrate that, for young adults, the ‘best place’ to get married may depend largely on when they hope to marry. Those who are committed to marrying in their twenties may want to think carefully about moving to a major coastal city; meanwhile, those same cities could be an excellent option—though not the only choice—for marriage-minded adults in their thirties," the study notes.

While coastal cities have lower marriage rates for 20-somethings, the picture changes for singles in their 30s. For adults ages 30 to 39, regions with the highest marriage rates include portions of the New York, San Jose, Los Angeles and Chicago metropolitan areas, along with suburbs in Texas and Indiana.

POLL FINDS SHARP RISE IN YOUNG MEN CALLING RELIGION 'VERY IMPORTANT'

Wang also explained that the research shows living in an area with a large population of single young people may not improve the odds of finding a future spouse.

"If you think your best chance of finding someone to marry is in the places with the most singles, think again," Wang told Fox News Digital. "The nation’s top 10 areas with the highest share of singles (more than 80% unmarried) are far from the places where most new marriages are happening."

The IFS research found that areas with more single men relative to single women tend to have higher female marriage rates, but the relationship is even stronger when researchers measure the ratio of full-time-employed single men to all single women.

Military-adjacent regions like Oceanside, California, and Fayetteville, North Carolina, as well as tech-heavy areas such as Mountain View and Sunnyvale, California, have some of the highest ratios of full-time-employed single men to single women.

DRIVEN BY PROGRESSIVE DOOMISM, LIBERALS ARE HAVING FEWER BABIES THAN CONSERVATIVE FAMILIES

However, the link between male income and marriage rates varies by age. For women in their thirties, regions with a higher ratio of single men earning at least $60,000 a year had higher marriage rates. That financial link disappears for women in their 20s, suggesting younger couples place less emphasis on high salaries when deciding to tie the knot. 

Still, on an individual level, young men in their 20s who earn $60,000 or more are about twice as likely to marry as lower earners. 

"Single men’s jobs remain one of the strongest factors driving marriage in America," Wang added. 

Regional marriage rates for young adults in their 20s also showed a strong positive correlation with areas that backed Donald Trump over Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. However, for adults in their 30s, this correlation flips and turns negative.

"One possible explanation is that more rural parts of the country, where Trump generally performed better than Harris, often have higher marriage rates for adults in their twenties," the study notes.

The researchers noted that their findings show broad regional patterns, not proof that a particular location or political environment causes people to marry.

The study measures where respondents currently live, not necessarily where they met their spouses or lived when they got married. The researchers also acknowledged that some people may have moved after marrying, potentially affecting the marriage rates of certain regions.

item.title: What a smart firewall does and why it matters on home Wi-Fi
item.description: Router firewalls and software firewalls serve different roles in protecting your home Wi-Fi from unwanted traffic and suspicious connections.
item.content:encoded:
Most of us think of home Wi-Fi as the invisible connection that lets a laptop stream a movie, a phone display photos and a printer work from across the room. In practice, it is also the meeting point for many devices, accounts and types of information. A typical home network may include computers, phones, tablets, smart speakers, televisions, cameras, printers and connected appliances. These devices regularly send and receive data.

Some of that traffic is expected, such as opening a bank website or downloading a software update. Other traffic may be unwanted or suspicious. That is where a firewall comes in. A firewall is a security system that checks network connections and applies rules about which traffic should be allowed. Think of it as a doorman for digital connections. It does not know everything about every visitor, but it can help prevent some unexpected traffic from reaching a device.

Understanding how firewalls work, where they fit and what they can and cannot protect against can help you make smarter choices about securing your home Wi-Fi.

FBI SAYS RUSSIAN HACKERS HIJACKED OLD WI-FI ROUTERS

Your router is the box that connects your home to the internet and sends Wi-Fi throughout the house. Many home routers include a built-in firewall. Because it sits at the gateway, this router firewall can help protect devices connected to your home network from certain unwanted connections coming from the internet.

A router firewall is useful because one device can provide a basic layer of protection for the network as a whole. It can help reduce direct exposure for computers, phones and other connected equipment. However, its settings and capabilities depend on the router model, its software and how it was configured.

A software firewall runs on an individual device, such as a Windows PC or Mac. It can add another layer of awareness and control at the device level. This becomes especially useful when a laptop leaves home, connects to a different network or needs to distinguish between applications running on that computer.

TRAVEL MISTAKE PUTS PHONE, LAPTOP AND STREAMING ACCOUNTS AT RISK

The two types can work together. A router firewall and a software firewall serve different purposes. The router helps guard the network's front door, while the software firewall helps watch activity involving a particular device.

The terms sound technical, but the basic idea is straightforward.

Inbound traffic is data traveling toward your device. For example, a website may send information back to your browser after you request a page, or a remote computer may try to connect to a service on your network. Some inbound traffic is expected, especially when it responds to a connection you started. Other inbound traffic may be unexpected.

Outbound traffic is data leaving your device. Opening a webpage, sending an email, uploading a photograph or syncing a file all involve outbound activity. If an unfamiliar program tries to connect to the internet, that may also be outbound traffic.

CHEAP STREAMING BOX COULD HIJACK YOUR HOME INTERNET

A firewall may use rules, application information and other signals to decide whether a connection looks familiar or requires attention. Depending on the operating system and security product, it may alert you, allow the connection or block it. The goal is to help ordinary online activity continue while making unusual network behavior more visible and manageable.

Online banking and shopping place sensitive information at the center of ordinary internet use. You may sign in to a bank, enter a card number, review a medical bill or manage a retirement account from the same computer you use for entertainment.

BEWARE OF HACKERS SHOWING UP PRETENDING TO BE IT

Remote work adds another reason to pay attention. A home laptop may handle work documents, personal files and video meetings throughout the day. If an unfamiliar application begins communicating online, security tools that provide additional context can help you understand what the computer is doing.

A firewall cannot tell whether every website, email or message is honest. A scammer may persuade someone to visit a legitimate-looking page or approve an action that appears convincing. A firewall provides one layer of protection, while your decisions remain an important part of staying safe.

YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES

A firewall can help control certain network connections. It may reduce exposure to some unsolicited inbound traffic and help identify unusual activity involving applications. It can also add a layer of protection when a device connects to networks outside the home.

A firewall cannot make a weak password strong or determine whether someone is being tricked by a convincing text message. It also cannot replace antivirus protection, software updates, multifactor authentication, secure router settings or reliable backups.

No firewall can guarantee that files, accounts or devices will never be compromised. Some threats arrive through activity you intentionally start, such as opening a malicious attachment or entering information into a fake website. Other threats may exploit weaknesses in outdated software. Those situations call for additional defenses and safer habits.

HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS

A few simple router and Wi-Fi settings can strengthen your home network and reduce unnecessary security risks.

Start with the router. Use the security mode recommended by the manufacturer or internet provider and avoid leaving the administrator password at its default. The administrator password controls important router settings and should be different from the Wi-Fi password.

Install router firmware updates when they are offered. Firmware is the built-in software that helps the router operate. Updates may improve performance, fix problems or address security weaknesses.

Use a strong, unique Wi-Fi password. If your router offers a guest network, consider using it for visitors or devices that do not need access to your main network.

Review the list of connected devices occasionally so you know what is using your Wi-Fi. If you see a device you do not recognize, investigate it and change your Wi-Fi password if needed.

Consider replacing a router that no longer receives security updates or cannot support current security standards. Check the manufacturer's documentation rather than assuming that a newer Wi-Fi label automatically gives you stronger security.

A firewall works best as part of a broader security setup that protects your devices, accounts and important files.

Keep your operating system, browser, apps and router updated. Turn on automatic updates when that option is available.

Use multifactor authentication for banking, email and other important accounts. Multifactor authentication adds a second verification step, such as an approval on your phone, after your password.

Be cautious with unexpected links, attachments and urgent requests for payment or personal information. Scammers often rely on urgency to get you to act before you have time to question what is happening.

Before approving a remote-access request, confirm who is asking and why. If an alert appears, read it carefully rather than automatically allowing or dismissing it.

Firewalls, antivirus software and backups each protect you in a different way. A firewall helps control network connections, antivirus software detects and responds to malicious software, and reliable backups can help you recover important files if they are damaged, deleted or locked by ransomware. Together, these protections create a stronger defense than any one tool can provide alone.

When choosing antivirus protection, look for real-time malware and ransomware detection, phishing protection, automatic security updates and coverage for all the devices you use. Some products also include device-level firewall protection or cloud backup, but features, storage limits and compatibility can vary by platform.

Visit CyberGuy’s best antivirus protection guide for our current recommendations, comparisons and special offers for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

Your computer may hold years of family photos, tax returns, medical records, scanned IDs, insurance documents and other files that would be difficult or impossible to replace. That makes protecting your data just as important as protecting the computer itself.

Ransomware is malicious software that can lock or encrypt your files and then demand payment to restore access. A firewall may help block or limit some suspicious connections, but ransomware can reach a device in other ways. Strong security habits and reliable backups give you a better chance of recovering if something goes wrong.

A useful guideline is the 3-2-1 backup strategy: keep three copies of important data on two different types of storage, with at least one copy stored separately from your computer. CISA guidance recommends this approach as one way to improve your ability to recover from ransomware.

Backups work best when they are automatic, current and separated from the same incident affecting your computer. Test a few backed-up files occasionally to make sure you can open them. When practical, keep at least one backup disconnected from your computer or otherwise isolated from routine activity. CISA recommends offline backups because some ransomware can also reach connected storage. Protect cloud backup accounts with strong, unique passwords and multifactor authentication. Norton AntiVirus Plus includes 2 GB of PC Cloud Backup on eligible Windows systems.

If your files suddenly become encrypted, disconnect the affected computer from the network if you can do so safely. CISA recommends isolating affected systems, including disconnecting them from Wi-Fi when necessary, to help prevent the infection from spreading. Avoid rushing to pay a ransom or deleting potential evidence. Preserve messages and notes about what happened and check whether clean backups are available. Consider contacting a qualified cybersecurity professional for help. If you believe an account may also have been exposed, change important passwords from a separate, trusted device.

FCC ROUTER RULE RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT FUTURE UPDATES

A firewall does a lot of work you may never see, and that is exactly why it can be easy to overlook. Your router firewall helps protect the network at home, while a software firewall can watch connections involving a specific computer wherever you take it. I would use both when available, but I would never count on a firewall by itself. Strong passwords, multifactor authentication, current software, antivirus protection and dependable backups all cover risks that a firewall cannot handle. The bigger point is visibility. Most of us have dozens of connections happening behind the scenes every time we use a computer. A good firewall gives you another set of eyes on that activity and another opportunity to stop something suspicious before it goes further.

item.title: Locals torch migrant shelters as Spain's PM points blame beyond the border
item.description: Ceuta residents burned migrant shelters as Pedro Sánchez accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks of spreading disinformation that fueled the crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Residents in Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta tore down and burned makeshift migrant shelters amid escalating tensions over a massive influx from neighboring Morocco, as Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks of helping spread disinformation that fueled the crisis.

Demonstrators carrying Spanish flags moved toward beachside migrant camps last week, destroying shelters and setting fires as police attempted to keep protesters and migrants apart, according to Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE and news agency EFE. Protesters chanted "Invasores, expulsión" — "Invaders, expulsion" — as they advanced toward the beaches where migrants have been staying, EFE reported Aug. 27.

Hundreds of residents returned to the streets the following day, marching toward the Trampolín and Benítez beach areas where migrants were camped and repeating the same chant, according to EFE.

The unrest follows an unprecedented surge on July 30 and 31, when more than 72,000 migrants irregularly crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, one of the European Union’s two land borders with Africa. At least 100 people died attempting the crossing, according to Ceuta authorities cited by Reuters on Aug. 31. Roughly 5,000 migrants remained in the enclave as of Monday.

STATE DEPARTMENT RAISES TRAVEL WARNING FOR PART OF SPAIN AS MIGRANT SURGE SPARKS MILITARY DEPLOYMENT

Sánchez on Monday directly linked the mass crossing to what he described as a foreign-backed disinformation campaign.

Spanish authorities have said misleading videos and posts circulating on Instagram, TikTok and other social-media platforms falsely suggested that migrants who reached Ceuta by sea would be permitted to remain in Spain.

CEUTA MIGRANT SURGE EXPOSES SPAIN-MOROCCO TENSIONS AS ISLAMIST GROUPS REPORTEDLY SEEK TO EXPLOIT BORDER CRISIS

Sánchez told radio station SER that research by the European Union’s diplomatic service, the European External Action Service, indicated Russian and Israeli networks had participated in spreading the disinformation alongside far-right networks, Reuters reported Aug. 31.

He argued that Russia and Israel had seized on the crisis to attack Madrid because of disagreements with his government over the wars in Ukraine and Gaza.

However, Sánchez provided no further details about the evidence supporting the accusation, according to the reports.

Both governments rejected his claims.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar accused Sánchez of "lying shamelessly" and said in a post on X that the Spanish leader was attempting to divert attention from domestic policy failures.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov separately rejected Spain’s accusation that Russia was connected to the Ceuta migration crisis.

Sánchez also rejected allegations that Morocco’s government deliberately facilitated the border surge, telling SER, "When people talk and speculate about the participation of Moroccan authorities, I deny this outright," according to Reuters. Spanish opposition parties and some human-rights organizations have accused Rabat of allowing the crossings, an allegation Morocco denies.

SPANISH JOURNALIST SAYS CEUTA RESIDENTS BELIEVE GOVERNMENT ISN'T DOING ENOUGH TO PREVENT ANOTHER MIGRANT RUSH

The disinformation surrounding the Ceuta crossing had been building well before Sánchez publicly accused Russian and Israeli-linked networks. Fox News Digital reported Aug. 4 that an open-source investigation by Golden Owl Intelligence traced weeks of activity across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that circulated misleading interpretations of Spanish immigration law, along with information about routes, meeting points and recommended crossing times.

The campaign intensified after Spain’s Supreme Court issued a July 8 ruling restricting the immediate return of migrants intercepted at sea near Ceuta and Melilla. Simplified accounts of the ruling, combined with confusion over Spain’s separate plan to regularize hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants, were circulated online as evidence that migrants reaching Spanish territory would be allowed to stay.

SPAIN'S MIGRANT SURGE REIGNITES DEBATE OVER EUROPE’S ISLAMIST TERROR THREAT

Zineb Riboua, a research fellow at the Hudson Institute, said at the time that Islamist movements were also seeking to exploit the crisis politically. Riboua argued that Islamist voices in Morocco and Spain were amplifying the unrest and portraying Europe as an attractive destination while using Morocco’s ties with Israel and the U.S. to attack the Moroccan government. In a July 31 analysis, Riboua wrote that Islamist activists had spent years encouraging young Moroccans to believe their country offered them little future and depicting Europe as a place where prosperity and opportunity were easily available.

The crisis has also spread beyond Spain. Italy on Monday extended for another 15 days its suspension of Schengen free-movement arrangements with Spain, a step first imposed July 31 in response to the mass influx into Ceuta.

Nile Gardiner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, warned Fox News Digital at the outset of the crisis that Ceuta could become "a key turning point in the unraveling of the European Union." "Once you unravel Schengen — which I think is inevitable — this breaks down the entire European project," Gardiner said.

Reuters contributed to this story.

item.title: FRANK SILLER: 'I love you, brother' -- the 9/11 loss that inspired a mission of service
item.description: Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller recounts the devastating 9/11 phone call from Richie Obermeyer at Ground Zero that confirmed his brother Stephen would not come home.
item.content:encoded:
PROGRAMMING ALERT: Watch Tunnel to Towers Chairman and CEO Frank Siller discuss his new book "Let Us Do Good," on "The Five" on Sept. 1 on Fox News Channel at 5 p.m. ET.

There are moments in life that divide everything into before and after. For me, one of those moments came on September 11, 2001, when a firefighter calling from Ground Zero told me what I already feared but was not ready to hear: my younger brother Stephen was not coming home. In that instant, my family’s life changed forever, and so did the course of mine.

Even though I knew that it was probably an exercise in futility, I also kept trying to call Stephen from my Nextel phone, on September 11, hoping that perhaps he had somehow already made it over the Verrazzano Bridge and back to Staten Island. We had the same phone; it was both a cellular phone and a walkie-talkie, which was popular in the early 2000s.

I kept pressing the button on the walkie-talkie part while I called out for Stephen. He did not pick up. I called again, and again, and again. There was no answer—only an eerie silence. I wound up doing that all night and well into the next few days.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

Once I got home to join Pat, early in the afternoon, family members began to straggle one by one through my front door. All we could do was sit in my living room and watch the news, just as hundreds of millions of our fellow Americans did that day. I felt like I was dreaming. It was all so surreal, especially since much of the carnage had occurred in my beloved New York City.

While it was tempting to excuse myself to go shed a few tears, I understood the need to be strong. I had already deep down accepted the harsh reality of Stephen’s fate and needed to be ready for the moment when other members of my family would soon be sadly forced to do the same—or maybe some already had.

AMERICA’S HEARTLAND COMES FACE-TO-FACE WITH 9/11 HISTORY AS 25TH ANNIVERSARY NEARS

That was when my home phone rang. I snuck off into the kitchen to quietly take the call, as not to alarm any family members. On the other end of the line was a neighborhood firefighter named Richie Obermeyer, who lived a few houses away from Stephen. He was calling from the area that would soon be known to America and the world as Ground Zero.

Unbeknownst to me, my daughter Elizabeth was watching me take Richie’s call from the hallway. Years later, she gave me her perspective of this exact moment. That’s the thing about tragedy—everyone has their own recollection and personal memory of the way things unfolded.

"Hi Frank, it’s Richie Obermeyer. I’m down here at the Twin Towers . . ." he said.

"Rich, I’m so sorry. That must be terrible," I said. "It’s just so hard to watch."

"Frank, it’s really bad," said Richie.

"I’m watching it—" I began to say.

"No, Frank." He hesitated and sighed. "It’s really bad."

Speaking slowly yet firmly, I tried to tell Richie that I understood while also hoping that he would have the courage to tell me the truth instead of making me ask him point-blank. That’s when Richie finally said it.

9/11 STEEL BEAM ARRIVES AT FLORIDA SCHOOL WHERE BUSH LEARNED AMERICA WAS UNDER ATTACK

"No one is coming home, Frank," Richie whispered. "No one."

I could hardly breathe. My chest started to tighten, and my eyes welled up. I then dropped my head, and tears began rolling down my cheeks. I already knew deep down that my brother was gone, but hearing the news from someone I trusted ushered in a whole new wave of emotion.

AS AMERICAN PRIDE HITS A 25-YEAR LOW, A NEW 9/11 EDUCATION PLATFORM URGES THE NATION TO NEVER FORGET

After I hung up the phone and took a deep breath, I walked into the living room to explain what Richie had told me. Elizabeth jumped into Pat’s arms. My sister Regina let out a startling shriek and yelled, "Not Stephen!"

We all felt the same way. How could this have happened to Stephen, our little brother who went through so much in life at such a young age? Not Stephen. Not Stephen, the resilient little boy who became an orphan at the age of ten. His five children—Katherine, Olivia, Genevieve, Jake, and baby Stephen—would now have to live their lives without their father, who was a most spectacular human. Stephen’s wife, Sally, the love of his life, would have to raise these children on her own, perhaps never filling the void Stephen’s death would leave in her heart and soul. How would she do it, emotionally, physically, and financially? It all seemed so impossible.

BENJAMIN HALL TACKLES GRUELING ONE WORLD TRADE CENTER CLIMB ON PROSTHETIC LEGS TO HONOR FALLEN HEROES

Moments later, we began hugging each other while the tears continued to fall from our eyes. It was truly gut-wrenching. We pulled ourselves together, said a prayer while we were on our knees. One by one, we stood up, bundled into our cars, and drove over to Sally’s house to be together as one family and pledge our everlasting love and support for Sally and the children.

When the sun came up on the morning of Tuesday, September 11, 2001, I couldn’t wait to get out onto the golf course with George, Russell, and Stephen. Like I said, the four Siller brothers didn’t get to do this often anymore.

As the sun went down on that unimaginably painful Tuesday evening, I repeated the last words I said to Stephen less than twenty-four hours before he became one of the nearly three thousand innocent people killed in the worst terrorist attack in American history.

"I love you, brother," I whispered. "See you tomorrow."

He had already finished his shift. When he turned his car around to return to his firehouse, FDNY firefighter Stephen Gerard Siller sacrificed his tomorrows so countless others could have their todays. When I later found out the full details of his ultimate sacrifice, it only enhanced my admiration and awe of what Stephen and his fellow first responders so bravely did on that awful morning.

Our parents, Mae and George Siller, were devout Catholics and members of the Secular Franciscan Order. We grew up under the guiding philosophy of Saint Francis of Assisi, who famously wrote that "while we have time, let us do good." They were words that all of us lived by, but especially Stephen, as evidenced by his last moments on earth.

Stephen’s life and heroic death serve as a reminder to us all to live life to the fullest and to spend our time here on earth doing good—this is his legacy.

"A single sunbeam is enough to drive away many shadows," is a quote often attributed to Saint Francis that illustrates how I feel about Stephen’s impact.

In the shadows of the collapsed Twin Towers, the memory of my fallen brother helped guide me and all the siblings toward that light. Starting on September 12 and continuing every day thereafter, Stephen’s mission to do good would be my family’s mission as well. God willing, a few others would be willing to help along the way. I never could have imagined just how many kind and generous souls would end up joining the cause.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

To honor Stephen’s memory and the sacrifice of so many that day, my family started the Tunnel to Towers Foundation to carry forward the way he lived his life: by doing good and helping others. His sacrifice became our mission, and today T2T continues that work in service of America’s heroes and their families. To learn more, visit T2T.org

item.title: White House brings receipts after media claims noncriminal ICE arrests ‘soaring’: ‘False narratives’
item.description: The White House says many ICE arrests labeled "noncriminal" by the Washington Post and New York Times involve MS-13 members and foreign fugitives.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: The White House and Department of Homeland Security are pushing back on "false narratives" being advanced by the mainstream media and bringing the receipts after the Washington Post and New York Times reported that noncriminal ICE arrests are skyrocketing under President Donald Trump.

The Washington Post reported last week that ICE is arresting "soaring numbers" of "noncriminal" illegal immigrants. The outlet said the agency had "detained more people without a criminal record this year than in all of 2025." The New York Times took a similar line, reporting that "ICE arrests soar as people with no criminal record are increasingly targeted."

However, Lauren Bis, a special assistant to the president and White House spokeswoman, told Fox News Digital that though "nearly 70% of illegal aliens arrested by ICE have been convicted or charged with a crime in the United States," the "actual arrests of public safety threats and criminals is much higher." This, she said, is due to many of the "noncriminal" illegal immigrants arrested by ICE having prior criminal history in their home country, including murder, child sex abuse and gang activity.

"These are just a few of the media's ‘non-criminals,’" said Bis, adding, "Why does the mainstream media continue to peddle false narratives protecting criminal illegal aliens?"

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

Fox News Digital reached out to the Washington Post and New York Times for comment.

According to the Department of Homeland Security, "Nearly 70% of illegal aliens ICE arrested across the country have criminal convictions or pending criminal charges just in the U.S."

The agency said, however, that this statistic "doesn't account for those wanted for violent crimes in their home country or another country, INTERPOL notices, human rights abusers, gang members, terrorists" and other offenses in foreign countries.

While DHS has emphasized that entering the country unlawfully constitutes a crime, the agency has previously shed light on some of the serious criminal charges of individuals considered noncriminal arrests.

This May, Homeland Security Investigations arrested Salvadoran national Josue Saul Garcia-Lopez, who, despite not having a U.S. criminal record, had an international warrant showing him as an active member of the foreign terrorist organization MS-13 and had been involved in extortion and robbery schemes in El Salvador for several years.

NEW YORK TIMES TORCHED FOR ‘FALSE’ REPORTING ON ICE INVESTIGATIONS, OUTLET FIRES BACK

Just days before, ICE had also arrested a Honduran national named Fredy Alexander Lopez Lara, who had an international warrant for homicide in his home country.

Another MS-13 member, Salvadoran national Danny Granados-Garcia, was arrested by ICE in April. He was wanted in his home country for murdering a pastor.

In March, San Diego Sector Border Patrol agents arrested Mexican national Salvador Suazo-Garcia in Lemon Grove, California, processed him administratively, and turned him over to Mexican authorities. Suazo-Garcia entered the U.S. legally in May 2021 under the Biden administration. He was wanted in Mexico for lewd and lascivious acts upon a child.

Shortly before Suazo-Garcia’s arrest, Border Patrol agents also arrested a female illegal immigrant from Mexico named Silvia Del Rosario Torres-Castro, who was wanted in her home country for homicide.

Late last year, ICE arrested Antonio Israel Lazo-Quintanilla, a Salvadoran national who is a member of another foreign terrorist organization called the 18th Street Gang. DHS said that "while technically his only crime in the United States is driving without a license," Lazo-Quintanilla was on El Salvador’s most wanted gang members’ list and was wanted for aggravated homicide, extortion, possession of drugs and other felonies. Lazo-Quintanilla’s mugshot showed his face covered in tattoos, including the numbers "666" across his forehead.

Months before that, DHS said that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested Mexican brothers Pedro Luis Ortiz-Mendez and Jose Vicente Ortiz-Mendez in Texas. Both brothers are wanted for multiple murders tied to an attack on a festival in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, where at least one victim was shot and another victim was attacked with a machete.

BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AFTER DEMOCRAT CHRIS MURPHY CLAIMS ICE IS ‘TERRORIZING LITTLE KIDS’

Bis said that "these are just a few examples of murderers, gang members, and pedophiles the media refers to as ‘non-criminals’ because they only have criminal records in their home country."

"No one would want these heinous criminals to be their neighbors," she said. "From foreign fugitives, gang members, and terrorists, ICE is getting the worst of the worst off our streets and out of our country."

item.title: Majority of Americans reject Trump’s renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America, poll finds
item.description: A Reuters/Ipsos poll shows 63% of Americans oppose Trump's executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America amid the U.S.-Canada trade war.
item.content:encoded:
A new poll has found that a majority of Americans oppose President Donald Trump’s decisions to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America and impose higher tariffs on Canadian goods.

In the 3-day Reuters/Ipsos poll that ended Sunday, 63% said they opposed renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, compared to 14% in favor. The rest were undecided or skipped the question.

The survey also found that 57% opposed new tariffs on Canadian goods, compared to 20% who supported the measures.

When asked by Fox News Digital for reaction, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said, "Canada has been a bad neighbor by ripping off our country for years.

"President Trump promised voters that he would not allow our country to be taken advantage of anymore, which is why he is fighting so hard to protect American industries and workers. Thanks to the President’s bold leadership, we are putting America back on the map," she added.

TRUMP'S CANADA TARIFF FIGHT REACHES CRITICAL POINT AS HOUSE GOP SUMMONS TRADE CHIEF

Trump last Thursday signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, a move that came during a trade war with Canada.

"The Lake of America was something I've been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico — we changed it — and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America," Trump said in the Oval Office.

The president said he directed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and the department to update the Geographic Names Information System to reflect the name change.

The order called Lake Ontario a "tremendous asset" to the United States.

TRUMP URGES CANADIAN COMPANIES TO IMMEDIATELY MOVE TO US, SAYS 'I DON'T WANT CANADIAN ANYTHING'

"The United States is the greatest protector of the Great Lakes, including the body of water currently known as Lake Ontario," the order states. "Without the security and investment provided by the United States, this freshwater system would not be open for shipping, recreation, and responsible use to the same extent as it is today."

Trump later accused Ontario of ripping off American businesses in a post on Truth Social on Sunday, claiming Canada wants "to be treated like a state, but they aren't one."

"They’ve been ripping us off for decades, and it’s going to stop," Trump wrote.

The U.S. imposed a 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods in late July, with the duties going into effect earlier this month. Canada responded with its own tariffs of up to 50% on U.S. imports.

The Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted online gathered 1,023 responses from U.S. adults and had a margin of error of 4 percentage points.

Fox News Digital’s Louis Casiano and Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

item.title: Ex-NFL star Chad Ochocinco dishes his 'storybook' Super Bowl matchup for the 2026 NFL season
item.description: Chad Ochocinco wants a Rams-Bengals rematch at SoFi Stadium for Super Bowl LXI, saying Aaron Donald's return makes the Rams almost unbeatable.
item.content:encoded:
It’s never too early to think about Super Bowl winners, as we’re just one week away from the 2026 NFL season kicking off.

For Chad Ochocinco, he doesn’t want to jump the gun too early on his prediction for Super Bowl LXI before he sees how teams start playing in the regular season.

But, if it were up to him, he does have a "storybook" ending to the season he wishes to see happen at SoFi Stadium this upcoming February. And it’s the same Super Bowl matchup the stadium saw the last time it hosted the Super Bowl.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"For me, my storybook ending would be a rematch of the 2021 Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams and the Cincinnati Bengals again," Ochocinco told OutKick while highlighting his partnership with DraftKings.

It was quite the battle between these two teams in 2021, as Matthew Stafford and the Rams, who took a big risk landing the veteran quarterback from the Detroit Lions via trade that offseason, came out on top over Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

LOS ANGELES RAMS BETTING OUTLOOK: WHY ONE ANALYST IS ALL IN ON A SUPER BOWL WIN AT +550

Years later, no one could’ve predicted that Stafford would be coming off an MVP 2025 NFL season, and even crazier, Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on the Rams’ defensive line.

"Obviously, for Aaron Donald, I love the story. I love the story of him coming out of retirement," Ochocinco said. "I like it when you think about that team defensively and when you think about what they have offensively. They already have a high-powered offense. So, you add Aaron Donald coming back, you already have Myles Garrett. You have [cornerback] Trent McDuffie.

"I think everybody would have to get hurt for them to lose. I’m just being honest. It’s almost unfair the kind of team they have right now, it’s the kind of team you build, if you play Madden and you play Ultimate Team, that’s exactly what the Rams are. Offensively and defensively. So, I don’t see them really losing many games. Obviously, you’re going to have some games where you fall short. But I see them coming out of the [NFC} West easily."

But Ochocinco’s loyalty lies with his Bengals, the team he spent 10 of his 11 NFL seasons with and continues to believe in today.

As someone who never shies away from calling it like it is, Ochocinco loved watching Burrow "being very vocal about not being happy last year and still doing talking this year." Burrow, in a "cryptic format" as Ochocinco put it, made a point to Bengals management that he doesn’t like losing and wants pieces on both sides of the ball to get back to the Super Bowl, which came in just Burrow’s second season in the NFL.

The Bengals made sure to extend Burrow’s top receivers, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while keeping tight end Mike Gesicki in place as well. Coupled with running back Chase Brown and some fortification on the offensive line, Cincinnati has what it needs on offense, which was never really the question.

Could the Bengals’ defense, a pain point for this club for the last couple seasons, get upgrades to match the offensive firepower Zac Taylor’s team possesses? On paper, Ochocinco likes what he sees this time around, to the point where he assumes it’s Super Bowl or bust.

"For my Bengals, it’s a put-up-or-shut-up year," he said. "Listen, management has given him everything he needs. You got [Ja’Marr] Chase, you got Tee [Higgins]. They went and did what they needed to do in the offseason, especially defensively. So, he has to get it done. So, I’m assuming this has to be our year.

'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS

"It’s because Joe Burrow talked about his displeasures publicly in cryptic format. If you’re a player, you understand what he meant. ‘Listen, I take winning serious. Everywhere I’ve been, I’ve always won. The pieces I had around me gave me the opportunity to win, and I want to make sure you guys are aligned with my same core values when it comes to winning and competing and giving me the pieces that I need.’ They showed you offensively and defensively, getting you [defensive tackle] Jonathan Allen, getting Dexter Lawrence, getting [safety Bryan] Cook from Kansas City. We got some good DBs. Therefore, now that you’ve done all the talking, and management has answered your requests, now it’s your turn. It’s on you to stay healthy, stay upright and deliver."

Burrow has to stay healthy in Ochocinco’s eyes for the Bengals to get back to the Super Bowl, which seems obvious. However, Burrow’s injury bug struck once again last season, as he played just eight games one season after leading the NFL in passing yards (4,918) and passing touchdowns (43).

But then again, is there any team that can take out the Rams this year if they stay healthy?

"In a sense it is unfair," Ochocinco said. "But as great as Myles Garrett is, as great as Aaron Donald is, you have to have a scheme. You have to have a plan. You think about a player like Aaron Donald, you’re going to have to double-team somebody. I don’t know who it’s going to be – you’re going to have to pick your poison. Aaron Donald, the last time he played, he had a 20-sack season and he was double-teamed 64% of the team. And still had 20 sacks – that’s unheard of. Then, you have Myles Garrett coming off a 23-sack season. So, I mean, what do you do? When you have players like that come upfield so hard, I’m thinking about quick game. The ball has to come out quick, so they don’t have the time to be able to get to the quarterback. Also, running the ball, I think misdirection. You got to get them going one way and get them to stop their feet because they’re so good. It’s easy for me say what you need to do. It’s another thing to go out there and execute it in a structured environment. I’m not sure, but they have their hands full."

OCHO LOVES DRAFTKINGS GAMEDAY

We’ll see how the 17-game-plus season shakes out, but discussions and predictions like these with Ochocinco prove that football is back, and he’s excited to impact the fan experience with DraftKings.

"DraftKings Gameday," which will take place on Sept. 2, was announced on Monday with quite the activation as it celebrates the first football season with DraftKings Sports & Casino available in all 50 states. As a way to fuel fans with the return of football, DraftKings will be offering free gas, while supplies last, to passenger vehicles at select gas stations in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Detroit. Specific locations and event times will be announced separately.

"For me, I think it’s fun because who else would do something like this outside of DraftKings. This is a great touch for NFL fans to start the season," Ochocinco said. "We’re giving you free gas, so when your respective team plays, you’re fueled up to go. And word of mouth will be, ‘You won’t believe this? You know what DraftKings did? I was able to save money and get tickets to go to a game because they paid for my gas.’ That makes sense."

There will also be exclusive DraftKings Gameday promotions for customers, a customized in-app experience, in-person activations, a charitable donation through the DraftKings SERVES program, and a new campaign featuring Kevin Hart and Nick Jonas this season.

"It’s all about the fan experience, so some of the offers and luxuries throughout the season is what sets us apart from everybody else. I’m happy to be a part of them," Ochocinco said.

item.title: GIANNO CALDWELL: Sanctuary cities call it compassion. Patricia Fox calls it the ultimate price
item.description: Patricia Fox testified how sanctuary policies left daughter Carissa Aspnes minimally conscious while Colorado Medicaid denied her in-home nursing care.
item.content:encoded:
This week, Patricia Fox stood before the House Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement Subcommittee and told lawmakers what sanctuary policies actually cost a family.

"My daughter, Carissa, was hit on March 28, 2025, by an illegal alien," she testified. "She was launched head first into a concrete barrier. The driver and passengers of the vehicle fled. Never checking to see if my daughter was alive." She continued: "Despite her initial prognosis, Carissa survived. Praise God. But survived and recovered are not the same."

Sanctuary city and sanctuary state policies have been championed from coast to coast as the most compassionate, resolute action a city or state can take. But, no one has really asked what they cost the citizens who actually live there. Patricia Fox paid the ultimate price for sanctuary policies in Colorado.

GRIEVING MOTHERS SCORCH DEM LAWMAKER AFTER HE PIVOTS DURING HEARING TO ATTACK 'MAGA REPUBLICANS'

Carissa Aspnes was 22 years old and celebrating a new start. She had just returned home to Aurora, Colorado, from Chicago to launch a career as an esthetician, and on March 28, 2025, she climbed onto the back of a motorcycle to mark her birthday. Minutes later, an illegal immigrant from Venezuela, Valeria De Los Angeles Bermudez Marcano, ran a stop sign, crossed three lanes of traffic and slammed into the motorcycle. She and her passengers fled the scene, leaving Carissa unconscious on the road without checking whether she was alive.

Carissa survived. However, 18 months later, her mother is still living what survival actually looks like. Carissa underwent emergency surgery to remove part of her skull and relieve brain swelling. She is now minimally conscious, nonverbal, wheelchair-bound and fed through a G-tube. "Every morning, I use a Hoyer lift to raise my adult daughter out of bed because she can’t sit up, stand or get herself up," Patricia testified.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS HONORS ANGEL FAMILIES DURING NATIONAL CRIME VICTIMS WEEK, CALLS CRIMES 'COMPLETELY PREVENTABLE'

Carissa's physician says she needs two people to safely assist her. "Colorado Medicaid denied us in-home nursing," Patricia said. "So I figure it out." Medicaid denied the wheelchair Carissa actually needs, too. So Patricia blends her daughter’s food, feeds her through the tube, brushes her teeth, bathes her and administers her medications, all while learning to read pain in a daughter who can no longer tell her where it hurts.

The financial toll is staggering. Between emergency surgery, rehabilitation and the $3,000 to $4,000 a month in ongoing therapy, equipment, and care that insurance routinely denies, Patricia says Carissa’s medical bills already total seven figures. She has been trying to raise money to cover those expenses through a GoFundMe campaign. And the toll isn’t only financial. Patricia’s 19-year-old daughter has already begun preparing for the day she and her older brother must take over Carissa’s care. At 19, her future has been rewritten by a crash she had nothing to do with.

DHS BLASTS CALIFORNIA SANCTUARY POLICIES AFTER JAIL RELEASES ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED IN HIT-AND-RUN

"One collision created an entire family of victims," Patricia testified.

And justice never arrived. Prosecutors dropped every charge against Bermudez Marcano except a single reduced Class 5 felony. As part of the plea deal, she was ordered to pay $15,000 in restitution, but only for the motorcycle. For Carissa’s brain injury, her wheelchair, her feeding tube, her family’s shattered future, there was nothing. "A motorcycle received more justice than my daughter," Patricia testified.

EXCLUSIVE: ANGEL DAD FINDS ‘NEW PURPOSE’ WITH ICE AFTER DAUGHTER’S KILLING TURNED HIS WORLD UPSIDE DOWN

Bermudez Marcano was eventually deported, but only after Patricia’s family reached out directly to ICE’s Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement (VOICE) office, which was created to connect victims and their families with case updates, resources and support as they navigate the immigration enforcement process against the person who harmed them.

Meanwhile, Colorado projected roughly $127 million from its General Fund this year for a program called Cover All Coloradans, which provides healthcare to people who lack qualifying immigration status, Patricia told the committee. Those are a state’s fiscal priorities laid bare: money for healthcare coverage regardless of legal status, while a citizen who was maimed by someone with no legal right to be driving on Colorado’s roads fights her own state’s Medicaid program for basic nursing care.

OPEN BORDERS WERE INSANE, BUT POLITICIANS DIDN’T CARE. FAMILIES LIKE MINE PAID THE PRICE

Patricia Fox is not a political operative. She is a mother who has become fluent in her daughter’s facial expressions, movements and heart rate because that’s the only language Carissa has left. Yet she made the trip to Washington anyway, sharing her family’s story as one of the Angel Families whose lives were permanently altered by policies that hand driving privileges to people who have no legal right to be behind the wheel in the first place.

Carissa’s story is not isolated. Mary Ann Mendoza has spent over a decade fighting the same fight since an illegal immigrant driving the wrong way on an Arizona highway, three times over the legal limit, killed her son, Police Sgt. Brandon Mendoza, in 2014. Joe Abraham buried his 20-year-old daughter, Katie, after a previously deported illegal immigrant struck her car at nearly 80 miles per hour and fled the scene.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Roughly 19 states and Washington, D.C., now allow people to obtain a driver’s license regardless of immigration status, sometimes without requiring English proficiency to read a stop sign. This is not compassion. It is a public safety failure with a body count, and the families paying for it are the ones who did everything right. I started the Caldwell Institute for Public Safety and the Caldwell Foundation for Public Safety because I believe the safety of American citizens has to come before politics, on both sides of the aisle. Carissa Fox’s family should not have to choose between fighting Colorado Medicaid and fighting for their daughter’s dignity.

Every family in this piece did everything right. They followed the law, raised their children to do the same and still buried them or, in Patricia’s case, watched a daughter’s future disappear in an instant. Sanctuary policies didn’t protect Carissa, Brandon, or Katie. They protected the people who took everything from them. Until we stop calling that compassion, more families will learn the same lesson the hard way.

item.title: WWE star slyly reacts to former stablemates' incredible AEW debut at All In
item.description: Big E seemingly reacted to Kofi and Austin Creed's AEW World Trios Championship win at All In, calling his former New Day stablemates his "brothers."
item.content:encoded:
Big E, Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods were a part of a WWE stable known as the New Day and for over a decade they were the team to beat in the tag team division despite different iterations.

The New Day had seven WWE Tag Team Championship reigns among them and held the World Tag Team Championship for 483 days at one point. Despite Big E suffering a career-threatening injury, Kingston and Woods forged a path as a dominant team. The two won their last tag team titles at WrestleMania 41 and turned heel in their final run when they kicked Big E out of their group.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

WWE parted ways with Kingston and Woods earlier this year, officially ending their chapter with the company. But their impact on the pro wrestling industry remained strong and it was underscored with their debut with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) over the weekend at All In.

Now known as Kofi and Austin Creed, the duo joined Swerve Strickland in a fight for the AEW World Trios Championship. They were re-introduced as The New Level and came out to a raucous crowd at Wembley Stadium in London. The three men outlasted six other teams to win the title.

Big E, who still works for WWE in a broadcaster capacity, reacted to his former stablemates’ major accomplishment. He posted a cartoon that featured a sign with the words, "Look how far you’ve come," emblazoned on it.

"Take a second today to recognize your own progress. You’ve made it farther than you think," he captioned the photo.

As others commented on the post, he called Kofi and Creed his "brothers."

"If you’re two living legends that are undervalued, sometimes you have to go to London!" he wrote in a separate comment.

The sport of pro wrestling includes a wide range of promotions that features WWE and AEW at the top of the food chain. Wrestlers change promotions all the time as everyone in the industry deals with the ebbs and flows of the business. Kofi and Creed will likely have a successful run in AEW and it’s important for those on the outside to acknowledge that regardless of the company.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

The New Level aren’t resting on their laurels. The first AEW "Dynamite" after All In should be a doozy and Kofi and Woods are set to play a role in that.

They will join Strickland in an AEW Trios Championship defense against The Rascalz – the group that features Dezmond Xavier, Myron Reed and Zachary Wentz.

AEW has a robust tag team division that was put on full display after Adam Copeland and Christian Cage defended the AEW Tag Team Championship against the Young Bucks.

FTR (Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler), The Motor City Machine Guns (Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley) and The New Level were all seen in the ring after the match. Every team is gunning for the tag titles but it was made pretty clear who the top contenders were on Sunday.

item.title: Sarah Ferguson plots bold return to Britain after Epstein scandal shattered reputation: expert
item.description: Sarah Ferguson is reportedly lined up for a tell-all TV documentary to share her side of the story after the damaging Jeffrey Epstein emails, according to royal experts.
item.content:encoded:
Sarah Ferguson has made a career out of comebacks — and after seven months largely hidden from public view, the former Duchess of York may be preparing for another.

Ferguson, 66, may be ready to step back into the spotlight, with one royal commentator describing the former Duchess of York as a "chameleon" who has repeatedly managed to reinvent herself.

"Sarah Ferguson is forever the chameleon," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "She always seems to bounce back."

SARAH FERGUSON IS HOPING 'TO EVAPORATE LIKE MIST' AS SHE'S SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 7 MONTHS: EXPERT

"The one person who believes in Sarah is Sarah!" Chard added.

One element of Ferguson's reported fresh start could be a new home in Britain. Chard said she understands Ferguson will be based in the Home Counties in a "£10,000 a month plush gated property with granny annex."

But a new residence may only be part of the attempted reset.

item.title: Logan Webb and Paul Skenes face off as struggling Giants visit Pirates in pitching duel
item.description: Logan Webb and Paul Skenes square off as the San Francisco Giants visit the Pittsburgh Pirates in a matchup of two underperforming 2025 clubs.
item.content:encoded:
Sports are fun for many reasons, but one main reason is that we expect one thing and then get something different. The idea that on any given night an underdog can beat a favorite, or that a bench player can have a career night, is what makes them so engaging. It can be incredibly frustrating as a sports bettor, but as a fan, it is awesome. As a sports bettor, there are a lot of people frustrated by these two teams and pitchers from this season as the Giants take on the Pirates.

The San Francisco Giants are one of the worst teams in baseball, which is quite surprising. The Giants are 57-81 for the season, and with their next loss, they will guarantee they are going to have a losing season. It was pretty unlikely they would go undefeated this month, but they are likely to lose between 90 and 95 games. This is another team in the league with plenty of talent, but they just couldn't put it together. Can it be blamed on their manager? The front office? Or is it just a lack of success from the pitching and offense combined?

I'd put most of the blame on the pitching staff as they carry a 4.34 ERA and a 1.35 WHIP into today's game. As usual with this pitching staff, the lone bright spot has been Logan Webb. This season, Webb is 8-8 with a 3.72 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. He is in a bad situation tonight, though. On the road, he has a 4.16 ERA, and in night games, he has a 4.98 ERA. Both are worse than his home and day starts. He did have a rather strong August with only one bad start. In four outings, he allowed four earned runs over 26 innings. In the lone bad start, he allowed five earned runs in 2.2 innings. The Pirates hitters haven't been great against him, with just 12 hits in 58 at-bats.

The Pittsburgh Pirates were expected to compete for a Wild Card spot this season, but it hasn't gone as expected. The team is just four games under .500, so they still have a chance to end the season at .500 or better, but the chances of them making the postseason are slim. The hitting has improved, and that is a big reason for the improvement overall for the team this year. However, the pitching staff hasn't performed as well as needed this season despite having high hopes.

It is easy to have high hopes for the team when you have the reigning Cy Young leading the roster. However, it has been a bit of a disaster season for Paul Skenes. Look, a lot of pitchers would love to have Skenes numbers - 9-11 record, 3.79 ERA, 1.12 WHIP, and 175 strikeouts. The WHIP and strikeouts are the better numbers, but his ERA and record are a bit rough. In his young career, this 3.79 ERA is two full runs higher than it was in his first two seasons. Skenes has been better at night and at home this season, so maybe he is in his optimal spot here. He had a decent August, going 20.1 innings over four starts and allowing just seven earned runs.

This is the first time Giants hitters are facing Skenes, so he definitely has an advantage. It almost seems improbable that no one on their roster has had an at-bat against him. item.title: Tampa Bay Rays look to capitalize on struggling New York Mets as Freddy Peralta faces former team

item.content:encoded:

The Mets won't be in the postseason, but today's opponent, the Rays, will be.

Francisco Lindor, Juan Soto, Bo Bichette, Luis Robert Jr., etc. These are all guys that have All-Star appearances and a lot of success in the past, but for whatever reason it just hasn't been able to click for the team.

Overall, the Rays are batting .260 as a team, and they are only middle of the pack in runs scored, so they need to find a way to get more people across the plate, because they aren't struggling to get guys on base.

item.title: Israel captures top Hamas commander in Gaza strike, defense minister says
item.description: Israel Katz says IDF forces captured Hamas security chief Mu'in al-Arabid during a deep raid in Gaza, with airstrikes covering the withdrawal.
item.content:encoded:
The Israel Defense Forces captured Hamas' head of general security during a raid in Gaza, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said.

An Israeli security official identified the Hamas leader as Mu'in al-Arabid, head of the General Security Apparatus, saying he was arrested during an Israeli incursion deep inside Hamas territory in Gaza. The IDF carried out airstrikes to cover the raid's withdrawal, adding that there were no Israeli casualties.

"A short time ago, a senior Hamas terrorist was arrested, and this is our policy: We do not wait for threats. Instead, we pursue Hamas terrorists, thwart them, and destroy their terrorist infrastructure. We have built a strong and unprecedented security zone in Gaza to protect residents and IDF soldiers," Katz said in a statement.

HAMAS STRUGGLES TO FILL LEADERSHIP RANKS AS ISRAEL HUNTS OCT 7 TERRORISTS

"Nearly 70% of the Gaza Strip has been destroyed, with no residents, no tunnels, and no homes, and the IDF controls the territory. We are not leaving Gaza until the Strip is demilitarized, Hamas is disarmed, and all terrorist tunnels are destroyed. Even after that, the IDF will remain in Gaza along defensive lines and ensure the security of the western Negev communities. Any attempt to bypass the security zone through aerial launches will be met with a harsh response," he added.

The raid comes weeks after President Donald Trump's administration demanded that Hamas disarm and give up control of Gaza in August. Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, traveled to Israel last month and said the IDF may receive U.S. backing to "finish the job."

NETANYAHU REJECTS BOARD OF PEACE'S GAZA PLAN: NO 'WITHDRAWAL UNTIL HAMAS IS GENUINELY DISARMED'

"If they don't follow through now on their commitment, everyone will see that they're not genuine about peace, and then Israel will have a lot more support from the U.S. and others to go and finish the job in the appropriate way," Kushner also told Fox News' Trey Yingst of the terrorist group.

The warning from Trump’s son-in-law followed a rare face-to-face meeting with Hamas in Egypt — only Kushner's second known meeting with the group.

KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL

"They said all the right things, but obviously, it's very, very hard to trust, you know, a terrorist organization that committed these terrible atrocities," Kushner continued. "But we had a very cordial meeting, and they said all the right things, and so we're going to give them a chance to perform."

"It's going to have to be based on actions and steps, and I hope it will be true."

The U.S.-led "Board of Peace" proposal centers on a phased ceasefire, demilitarization of Gaza, Israeli troop withdrawal, Palestinian technocratic governance and international reconstruction efforts.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Grandfather finds hidden treasure in plain sight as park officials 'dumbfounded' by discovery
item.description: A man from Tennessee found a 2.29-carat yellow diamond at Crater of Diamonds State Park while on a diamond search with his two granddaughters in Arkansas.
item.content:encoded:
A grandfather from Tennessee recently walked away from an Arkansas state park with a remarkable discovery: a yellow diamond.

He made the discovery at Crater of Diamonds State Park in Pike County, Arkansas State Parks announced Aug. 29.

At the time, Barry G. Smith of Germantown, Tennessee, was searching for diamonds in the park with his two granddaughters, Sage and Juniper.

STUNNED COUPLE UNEARTHS 150-POUND MYSTERY HIDDEN BENEATH THEIR BACKYARD FOR DECADES

​"Not expecting anything more than a fun time, the family rented a wagon and basic kit from the park and began their diamond search," Arkansas officials said in a statement about the Aug. 16 discovery.

After about 30 minutes of searching, Smith spotted something glimmering in the East Drain section of the park — but initially mistook it for mica, a glittery and common mineral.

The grandfather placed the gem in his shirt pocket and didn't think much of the find until he had it inspected at the park's Diamond Discovery Center, he said. 

"After further inspection, staff confirmed that Smith had found a gorgeous 2.29-carat yellow diamond," the release said.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS FACE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES IN BOOK OF REVELATION CITY

The diamond surprised even park officials.

​"I was dumbfounded when I first saw the diamond," facility supervisor Ralph Hall said in a statement.

"Its overall shape and color immediately reminded me of the Pearadin Schumacher American Dream Diamond found earlier this year," Hall added.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ARTIFACT DEPICTING PHARAOH THOUGHT TO HAVE CHALLENGED MOSES IN EXODUS

Park officials indicate that yellow diamonds rank as the rarest variety found in the park, with the majority of visitors discovering brown or white stones instead.

​"Yellow diamonds are created when nitrogen is absorbed into the crystal structure during formation," Arkansas State Parks noted.

"Nitrogen impurities absorb blue light and reflect yellow wavelengths, giving the diamond its yellow hue."

Smith told park officials he was "absolutely" excited about his discovery.

POLICE OPERATION TAKES UNEXPECTED TURN WHEN OFFICERS STUMBLE UPON ANCIENT BURIAL CAVE

"I never expected to find a diamond here," the grandfather said.

He added, "The potential was there, but you never come here expecting to find one."

Smith chose to name the gem the Sage Juniper Diamond, after his granddaughters.

Park officials described the diamond as about the size of a black-eyed pea, noting that it was the third-largest diamond found at the park this year.

"As of this publication, 351 diamonds have been registered by park guests in 2026," the release added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"An average of one to two diamonds is found at the park each day."

Officials did not release an estimated value for Smith's diamond.

Arkansas State Parks previously told Fox News Digital that park employees "are not trained to grade or appraise diamonds or other rocks and minerals."

An official said, "Anyone interested in having their diamonds graded or appraised can reach out to a certified gemologist, who has had special training to properly grade gemstone quality and estimate value."

Several notable diamonds have been discovered at the park in recent months.

Earlier this month, a grieving Pennsylvania woman discovered a 3.09-carat diamond just days after burying her father and months after losing her son.

A few months before, a Texas man unearthed a 2.09-carat brown diamond during a family trip inspired by his 7-year-old son's interest in mining for crystals.

5 TAKEAWAYS FROM FLORIDA SENATE PRIMARY: GOP SEN ASHLEY MOODY WILL FACE DSA'S NIXON

That sounds like communism to me. They’re taking over their oil reserves and wanting to sell them off. That is the epitome of what communism is, and that is what Ashley Moody is okay with. Nixon referenced Trump's announcement on Friday that the U.S. had reached an oil deal with Venezuela involving more than 65 billion barrels of proven reserves. The deal came after the United States launched an operation to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in January and began working with interim President Delcy Rodríguez.
